title: U.S. Plans Tighter Rules on High-Tech Money Sent Abroad
summary:
On Thursday, October 23, the U.S. Treasury Department proposed a new rule to tighten limits on U.S. high-tech investments in China, Russia, and North Korea. The rule is only a proposal, and Treasury will hear public comments before a final rule.

Outbound investment means money U.S. investors put into companies in other countries. The government says it has worked for years to stop such money from helping adversaries build up military power.

The proposal would add hypersonic systems that travel at five times the speed of sound, supercomputing, biotechnology, and artificial intelligence, which Treasury called superintelligence. It would apply only to investments over $50,000, and it would exclude many financial investments, including stock purchases.

The program began in 2023, when then-President Joe Biden signed an order limiting investments in semiconductors, quantum computing, and artificial intelligence going into China. In December 2025, Congress expanded the program to more technologies and countries.

Supporters say it shows Washington is watching where U.S. money goes. China pushed back, with spokesperson Mao Ning saying overstretching national security and restricting trade serve no one's interests.
why_it_matters: Rules about where money can go shape the technology in phones, computers, and games you may use one day.
